fm.folderHelp: The plugin writes archivix-snapshot.json to this folder (for example D:\Sports Interactive\Football Manager 27\archivix). Simloom only reads it and never touches your save.

saveFile.label: FM27 save
saveFile.help: Game save followed by this career (games folder, next to the plugin folder). Simloom only reads its name and date.
saveFile.other: FM27 has loaded a save with {{club}}, but this career follows {{expected}}: nothing is imported here. Open the Simloom career for that save, or import anyway if you changed clubs.
saveFile.free: Without a club since {{date}}: your next club will be picked up automatically

fm.empty: No squad imported yet. Start FM27 with the plugin, load your save, then click “Import from FM27”.

col.name: Player
col.starsHelp: Current / potential ability stars according to your staff

an.xiSub: best player in each position, out of 20
an.depthHelp: Natural players in each position. Red: nobody in a key position; amber: only one player.

sum.noMatch: Available with the latest plugin version.

bridge.title: FM27 plugin
bridge.intro: The plugin reads your squad in FM27 (read-only) and hands it to Simloom. Simloom installs and updates it for you.
bridge.gameMissing: fm.exe not found in this folder
bridge.bepinexMissing: BepInEx 6 (IL2CPP) is not installed: the plugin needs it.

bridge.offline: Could not check the latest version (offline?).

tac.noAttributes: Player attributes are needed: import again from FM27.
tac.localRefError: Local reference file unreadable: using built-in reference
tac.suggestedHelp: Placement worked out by Simloom. The plugin can't yet read which player holds each position in your FM27 tactic.
tac.pitchHelp: Eleven picked by fit to the style's roles, injured players left out. Dotted lines show the move from the other phase; hover a player to find them in the list.
tac.balanceHelp: Pace, pressing and aerial play are compared to your eleven's average level: green = strength, red = weakness. Each weakness lowers the team rating, which picks the formation and style: the eleven is judged as a whole, not only position by position.

width.title: Width
width.ok: someone provides width on each side

missing.L: no wide role on the left
missing.R: no wide role on the right
missing.both: no wide role on either side

width.tip: Put a wide role (full-back, winger) on that side or use “Play wider”.

creation.title: Creativity
creation.tip: Aim for 2 to 4 creative roles (deep-lying or advanced playmaker…).

cover.title: Cover
cover.tip: Keep a defensive midfielder or a screening role out of possession.

box.title: Box presence
box.tip: Add a role that attacks the box (inside forward, second striker…).

pace.title: Defensive pace
pace.textHigh: {{value}} on average for a high line
pace.tip: Too slow for a high line: drop it a notch.

press.title: Pressing
press.tip: Trigger the press a little less often to last 90 minutes.

aerial.title: Defensive aerial play
aerial.tip: Avoid defending deep against crossing teams.

tac.fromGameHelp: Players and positions read from your FM27 tactic. Roles and instructions: the game's when the plugin reads them, otherwise each player's best role in that position.
tac.suggestedHelpGame: Placement computed by Simloom for the chosen style. “Game XI” shows your real FM27 line-up.
tac.pitchHelpGame: Your FM27 line-up. Dotted lines show the move from the other phase; hover a player to find them in the list. Click a formation below to compare with an eleven worked out by Simloom.
tac.projectBest: Your project is now the best choice
tac.baseKeptHelp: Another tactic ({{other}}) rates slightly higher, +{{gain}} star, but it would take at least +{{need}} star to make up for the tactical understanding lost by switching. Your base stays; only the players change, match after match.
tac.teamHelp: Every card of the game's Team Instructions screen, in its order; in bold, those the style sets, the others stay on the default. Set them with the mentality.

xi.title: The eleven to set in FM27

tac.matchSame: Your base tactic, {{form}} {{style}}, remains the best against this opponent.
tac.matchBest: Against this opponent, play {{form}} {{style}} rather than your base tactic ({{base}}).
tac.matchHelp: Matchup inferred from the opponent's profile (formations, pressing, defence) with football rules. It starts from your base tactic: without a weakness measured in the game's report the formation stays, and a style change must gain more than the understanding it costs.
tac.matchHelpMeasured: Matchup measured on what the opponent concedes depending on the formation they face (game report), plus their profile.

why.coverStrikers: They play two strikers: two defensive midfielders (or three centre-backs) cover them.
why.thinCover: They play two strikers: with no defensive midfielder, your centre-backs are two against two.
why.winMidfield: Their midfield has two in the middle: with three centrally you win midfield.
why.widthVsScreen: Out of possession their two defensive midfielders close the middle: width pays off.
why.possessionVsLowPress: They rarely press: your short passing game will have time.
why.directVsHighPress: They press a lot: your direct game goes over the press.
why.attackLeaky: Their defence concedes often: an attacking mentality makes the most of it.
why.concedesMore: Against this formation they concede a clear-cut chance every {{every}} min ({{minutes}} min observed), more often than usual.
why.concedesLess: Against this formation they concede a clear-cut chance only every {{every}} min ({{minutes}} min observed).
why.changeForm: Changing formation costs tactical understanding (estimate: −0.3): only suggested on a weakness measured over at least 270 min.

team.label: Team
team.help: Team B: the best XI without Team A's starters, same formation and style, for rotation (cups, congested fixtures, fatigue). Team rating: A {{a}}, B {{b}}.

contracts.byYear: Monthly wages freed by contract end year
contracts.soon: Contracts to deal with (18 months or less)

wages.byStatusHelp: Statuses from highest to lowest. A healthy wage bill pays higher statuses more: the average should drop with the status.
wages.overText: {{wage}} per month, more than a typical “{{status}}” ({{ref}})
wages.underText: {{wage}} per month for a “{{status}}”, less than a typical “{{other}}” ({{ref}})
wages.releaseText: {{wage}} per month saved if he leaves
wages.valueHelp: Monthly wage per level point: most expensive first.

fin.unknown: not read by the plugin yet
fin.simHelp: Contracts ending within 12 months. Enter the wage you would offer (0 = let him go): the room is recalculated. Nothing is saved.
fin.effect: Effect on the wage bill: {{delta}} per month
fin.afterUnknown: the room will show once the board budget is known
fin.noBoard: Board expectations (league position, style, youth, finances) are not read by the plugin yet.

loans.none: No loaned-out players. They are read with the transfer targets (LireCibles setting, "pretes" source in chemins.json) when the game date changes.
loans.help: A young player who doesn't play on loan barely progresses: recall him or find another club next window.

dressing.unknown: not read by the plugin yet
dressing.noMorale: Player morale is not read by the plugin yet. Once it is, you will see who is unhappy and how it affects buy-in to your tactics.
dressing.leadersHelp: Sorted by Leadership then Determination. A leader with low morale weighs on the whole group.

cmp.help: Highlighted: best in the row. The reference role's key attributes are in bold. The list also includes the game's targets when the plugin provides them.

prog.title: Level since {{date}}
prog.snaps_one: 1 snapshot: {{dates}}. Import one at each new game date to see the curves.
prog.snaps_other: {{count}} snapshots: {{dates}}. Import one at each new game date to see the curves.

depth.help: Level today → {{s1}} → {{s2}}. The game hides potential: the projection follows the average age curve (strong up to 22, decline after 30), then the real trend once snapshots are several months apart.
depth.fromTactic: Same style, formation and XI as Tactics > Line-up: change them there and this view follows.
depth.fromGame: XI read from your FM27 tactic (or Simloom's if you pick it in Tactics > Line-up).

cal.help: Two matches 3 days apart or less: rotate the most tired players.
cal.none: The fixture list comes with the latest plugin version. Meanwhile, rotation is based on current condition and sharpness.
cal.rustyHelp: Give them minutes in cup games or late in matches to regain sharpness.

roles.help: Each cell shows the fit for the best {{phase}} role at that position. Pills: natural positions. Grey numbers: out of position (the game adds a familiarity penalty). Dashed circle: out of position but better than at his own, worth a try. Hover a cell to see the role.

how.keys: 70%: the role's key attributes, weighted by importance.
how.base: 20%: the position's basic attributes (for a centre-back: marking, tackling, heading, positioning…).
how.engine: 10%: "match engine" attributes (acceleration, pace, anticipation, decisions), useful everywhere outfield.
how.foot: Stronger foot: on a flank, −0.5 if the foot does not match (−1 if one-footed). Inverted roles want the foot opposite to the flank.

style.whichHelp: Each style's requirements compared with the profile of the 16 best available outfield players. Pick a style for details.
style.profileHelp: Average out of 20. Highlighted: what the selected style needs.
style.rolesHelp: Fit = weighted average of the role's key attributes. Injured players excluded.
style.effHelp: New in FM27: a gauge tells whether the team will carry out your instructions. Simloom estimates it here; the game's real gauges are under "Effectiveness" once the plugin reads them.
style.simplify: Simplify instructions or plan training time.
style.allClose: All styles are within {{gap}} of each other: your squad doesn't favour any. Pick your project's style; Simloom builds the best eleven for each.

eff.none: The game's effectiveness gauges are not in this snapshot yet. Meanwhile, Simloom's estimate is under "Playing style".
eff.snapsSub: import every week to track progress

proj.help: Simloom measures the gap between your squad and this style, then derives the positions to sign and each player's work. Natural formations for this style: {{forms}}.
proj.developSub: 23 or younger, close to the level

verdict.step: Gradual switch possible: keep {{rec}} and add instructions from your project.
verdict.no: Not yet: stay with {{rec}} for now.

c.readyHelp: positions at target level (7 of 11 advised)
c.abilityHelp: reading of the game vs. style complexity

proj.eta: With the same squad, a safe switch around {{date}}.
proj.etaNever: With the same squad, the switch does not happen within 3 years: you need to sign players.
proj.tipRecruit_one: Signing speeds everything up: {{count}} more ready position needed to reach 7 of 11.
proj.tipRecruit_other: Signing speeds everything up: {{count}} more ready positions needed to reach 7 of 11.
proj.tipBridge: Bridge style: {{bridge}} is almost as suitable as {{rec}} and closer to your project.
proj.tipGauge: In match, check the game's tactical effectiveness gauge before switching: it has the final say.
proj.switchHelp: Projection: each player progresses along the age curve (or his real trend), attributes shifted accordingly. Ignores departures and signings.
proj.noRecruit: No position to sign at this target level.
proj.recruitAll: For all signings, the style needs: {{list}}.
proj.collectiveMore: Also: team cohesion for buy-in, match preparation for the opposition report.
proj.trainingHelp: Target role: his position's role for a starter in the target XI, otherwise the project role he fits best. Areas: his 3 weakest key attributes for that role, for individual training.
proj.trainingDetail: The player-by-player detail (target role, attributes to work on, intensity) is in the next step, Training.

targets.title: Transfer targets · {{style}} {{form}}
targets.help: Players from your shortlist, your recruitment targets and those on trial, read from the game and kept in Simloom. For each one, Simloom tells what they would add to your target XI ("Recruitment and training"): starter if better than the current starter, backup if better than your current backup in that position, otherwise nothing. Click a name to compare.
targets.none: No targets yet. This needs FM27 plugin 0.4.0 with the LireCibles setting on: it reads your shortlist and recruitment targets on each new game day. Meanwhile, the profiles to look for are under "Recruitment and training".
targets.noneRead: The plugin read the game's lists but found no player ({{status}}). Add players to your shortlist, or check targetSources in the snapshot.
targets.gainHelp: {{gain}} fit points against the current starter

pi.title: Player instructions
pi.help: Picked from the player's attributes against their own level, position, foot, roles and the style. An instruction the game locks for the role is never suggested.
pi.locks: Locks inferred from the roles (screening, covering, dropping, outlet: pressing locked to “Less often”; pressing roles: “More often”). If you spot another padlock in game, say so and the rule will be extended.
pi.nothing: Nothing to add: the role is enough.
pi.switch: Role {{phase}}: switch from {{from}} to {{to}} to allow “{{what}}”.

why.gkShort: good with his feet, suits short distribution
why.rushOut: good rushing out, useful behind a high line
why.shootLess: weak shot: look for the pass
why.directPass: can find the space in behind

cutInside.LR: left foot on the right side
cutInside.RL: right foot on the left side

why.holdPositionFb: lacks pace and stamina to get forward
why.holdPositionDm: positioning and teamwork: shields the defence
why.roam: movement, vision and flair above their level
why.lateRuns: movement and shooting: good at arriving late
why.tackleLess: weak tackling: avoid fouls and cards

pi.budgetLow_one: At most {{count}} instruction per player for now: the group still lacks tactical ability for this style. More will come as it improves (see Development plan).
pi.budgetLow_other: At most {{count}} instructions per player for now: the group still lacks tactical ability for this style. More will come as it improves (see Development plan).
pi.budgetFull: At most 3 instructions per player: beyond that, complexity lowers tactical understanding.

phaseHelp.P: 4 weeks back: P1 and P2 physical only, P3 adds ball work (Wednesday and Saturday friendlies), P4 passing, build-up, attacking and defensive work (Wednesday friendly).
phaseHelp.T: 4-week block to install the tactic, with a Wednesday match.
phaseHelp.A: First 4 months: broad technical and tactical work.
phaseHelp.B: Next 3 months: established organisation, match preparation and team bonding.
phaseHelp.C: To the end: match preparation, defensive organisation and set pieces.
phaseHelp.R: Winter break: full week of rest, as in the game. The last weeks before the restart become a mini pre-season (P1 to P4, P4 just before the restart).

train.title: Training week
train.manual: This week's matches are unknown (the game only gives the next 5): tick the match days, friendlies included.
train.priorities: Areas of your target style worked first: {{list}}.
train.rule1: Day before a match: match preparation. Day after: Recovery, Recovery, then Team Bonding as the extra.
train.rule2: No Rest sessions: Team Bonding is not rest.
train.rule3: If a match moves, put preparation back the day before and recovery the day after.
train.rule4: Players back from international duty are handled separately.
train.rule5: Judge the plan over several weeks, not one result, and lighten it if the workload doesn't suit.
train.source: "Freedom" method (FM Scout, FM27 training schedules): 44 schedules, 4-week themed cycles. The article ships no .fmf files: Archivix rebuilds each day with FM27's sessions, steered by your target style. Copy it into the game's Training screen.
train.trainingDaysHelp: A part-time club only trains on some evenings: tick the days offered in the game's Training screen. Other days without a match stay free; the last session before a match is used for preparation.
train.presetHint: Starting point in the game: load the "{{preset}}" schedule, then adjust the sessions as below.
train.weakest: Least understood areas according to the game (Effectiveness), added to the priorities: {{list}}.

reason.veryTired: condition below 80%: the game lowers the intensity
reason.tired: condition below 90%: the game adjusts the intensity
reason.young: 21 or under and fully fit: double intensity, he improves the most
reason.veteran: 32 or over: let the game manage him
reason.normal: nothing to force: the game sets it by condition

train.rusty: lacking sharpness: reserve minutes or late appearances
train.individualHelp: Matches the game's Individual Training screen. IP and OOP roles: those of his slot in the target XI, otherwise the project role he fits best. Focus: the one that works his weakest key attribute for that role (below, his 3 weak points). Intensity: the team's, set by the game according to condition; the only exception is double intensity for fully fit players aged 21 or under outside two-match weeks.
train.noMentoring: No group to suggest: it needs players aged 21 or under and at least one player aged 24+ with a favourable personality (or high determination). Personality comes from the extended player read.
train.mentoringHelp: In the game: Training, Mentoring, Create Mentoring Group. The personality and determination of influential players rub off on the youngsters in the group, for better or worse. A group has at most 3 players: the mentor and 2 youngsters, from the same area of the pitch when possible.
train.setupHelp: Tick a player once their individual training is set in the game. As soon as the advice changes (condition, injury, busy week, target XI), the box unticks and the row moves to the top with the old setting struck through.
train.teamIntensityHelp: Recommended setting in Training > Team Intensity: the game then adjusts each player's intensity and rest by condition. No need to touch individual intensity, except for exceptions (a fully fit youngster on double intensity).
train.upcomingHelp: Set ahead in the game's Training Schedule screen: one Schedule Focus and one workload per week. Light in two-match weeks, medium with one match, heavy with no match and early in pre-season. Beyond the next known fixtures, Archivix assumes a Saturday match.

intro.home: What needs your attention today, the styles that suit the squad, your best players and your youngsters.
intro.squad: Every first-team player, sortable by level, condition, contract or wage.
intro.analysis: The squad diagnosis: priorities, lines, depth and age profile.
intro.stats: Each player's match stats (passes, xG, pressing, duels) and what they say to work on.
intro.compare: Two or three players side by side, from the club or your shortlist.
intro.loans: Your loaned-out players: where they play and whether they improve.
intro.tactic: The best formation and starting eleven available today, position by position.
intro.depth: Who plays in each position, and which backup could overtake within two seasons.
intro.calendar: Upcoming matches and who to rotate based on fatigue.
intro.roles: How well each player suits each position and role.
intro.effectiveness: The game's tactical effectiveness gauges and what to work on this week.
intro.style: Step 1: which playing style your squad can play today, and which one to aim for.
intro.project: Step 2: the eleven the target style needs, position by position: ready, to develop or to sign.
intro.training: Step 3: the team and individual training schedule that moves the squad towards the project.
intro.targets: Step 5: your in-game shortlist, ranked by what each player would add to the project.
intro.finances: Budgets, contract-extension simulator and board expectations.
intro.wages: Wages grouped by squad status, and what stands out.
intro.progression: Each player's level since the first snapshot.
intro.opponent: The next opponent as the game's team report describes it, and how to play them.
intro.mercato: Step 4: who to move on (sale, loan, contract end), who to renew, and which youngsters are worth it for the project.

opp.none: No report on the next opponent yet. The plugin reads it on its own once chemins.json holds the « adv… » reads (opponent step 1).
opp.adviceHelp: Football advice drawn from the opposing manager's profile and key players, read from the game's team report. These are not game calculations.
opp.squadHelp: Opponent stars only show when your staff knows them.

advice.buildShort: They rarely press: build short from the back, your defenders will have time.
advice.beatPress: They press a lot: plan direct or long outlets to bypass their press.
advice.rotate: Man marking: make your players rotate and drop deep to drag their markers out of position.
advice.overloadZone: Zonal marking: overload one zone (a flank or the middle) to create numerical superiority.
advice.twoStrikers: Two strikers: keep at least three players behind the ball (a defensive midfielder, or only one full-back going forward).
advice.oneStriker: A lone striker: both full-backs can push on, two centre-backs are enough to cover him.
advice.betweenLines: Two banks of four with no attacking midfielder: put a player between their lines (attacking midfielder, false nine).
advice.counter: Attacking mentality: they will leave space behind, prepare quick counters.
advice.patience: Cautious mentality: expect a low block, move the ball and stretch the play.
advice.markCreator: {{name}} makes them tick: tight marking on him and cut his passing lanes.
advice.watchScorer: {{name}} is their goalscorer: give him no space in the box.
advice.screened: Out of possession, two defensive midfielders close the middle: attack down the flanks and behind their full-backs.
advice.leaky: Their defence concedes a clear-cut chance every {{name}} minutes: be ambitious and get bodies in the box.

opp.formsHelp: Read from the formation analysis of the game's team report. Out of possession, chances are those they concede.

memory.open: Trial: read the FM27 database directly
memory.title: Direct FM27 database reading (trial)
memory.intro: Simloom reads the game database in memory, from outside the game and read-only: nothing is written to FM27. Start FM27, load your save, then compare the values below with the in-game profiles.
memory.patched: Different game version: addresses found by patterns, to be checked

merc.help: Based on the imported squad, in two elevens: the one to play today ({{form}}) and the project one ({{style}} {{projectForm}}). At each position we keep the starters plus one backup per slot (two backup keepers); anyone beyond that is surplus. Stars are the staff's (current → potential, relative to the club); level is projected two seasons ahead.

kpi.incomeSub: value of players to sell · wages freed: {{wages}}
kpi.extendSub: starters and prospects within a year of expiry
kpi.offSub: profiles that don't suit the target style

merc.noYouth: No player aged 21 or under in the imported squad.
merc.youthHelp: A youngster is worth it when their profile suits the game plan and the staff rate their potential at 3 stars or more, when they catch the starter at their position within three seasons, or when they already make one of the two elevens. Blocked at 19 or older: loan them out to play. 18 or younger: they develop with the club's youth team. An off-project profile isn't worth the time, even with potential.

groupHelp.sell: No place in either eleven, not even as a backup: transfer-list them.
groupHelp.release: No place in either eleven and no market value: don't renew, or terminate to free the wage.
groupHelp.loan: Promising youngsters stuck behind starters and backups: a loan gets them minutes.
groupHelp.extend: Contract ending within a year: renew before they leave on a free.
groupHelp.replace: Starters today whose profile doesn't suit the project (or outside the project eleven at 27 or older): they play while they're the best, without a renewal, until a replacement who suits the target style arrives.
groupHelp.core: starters in today's or the project eleven.

why.misfit: less suited to the target style at {{pos}}
why.potentialPa: PA {{pa}}, the starter is at {{ca}} CA

stats.title: Data centre
stats.none: No match stats in the snapshot yet. They arrive with the plugin's next snapshot (stat* keys in chemins.json): advance one day in FM27.
stats.tooEarly: Fewer than 3 matches played: too early to judge the team.
stats.noAlert: Nothing alarming in the team's stats.
stats.help: Season stats, all competitions, as in the game's Data Centre. Each player is compared with players in his line: green = top quarter, coral = bottom quarter. Greyed out: under {{min}} minutes, not compared. "To work on" = individual training focus that targets his weakest match stat.

possession.text: Only {{value}}% pass completion: the team loses the ball too quickly for a control game.

creation.text: {{value}} xG per match: the team creates few chances.

pressing.text: {{value}}% of pressures won: the team presses without winning the ball.

duels.text: {{value}}% tackles won: the team loses its ground duels.

mistakes.text: {{value}} errors led to an opposition goal.

finishing.text: {{value}} goals versus xG: the forwards waste chances (individual focus "Chance conversion").

discipline.text: {{value}} cards per match: suspension risk, ask players to stay on their feet and tackle less hard.

stats.allNone: Full stats arrive with the plugin's next snapshot (updated chemins.json).
stats.allHelp: Current season, all competitions, as in the game's Data Centre (totals unless marked /90 or %).

legend.sort: Click a column to sort, hover it for its definition.

def.passPct: Share of attempted passes that reach a teammate.
def.progPass90: Passes that clearly move the ball towards goal, per 90 minutes.
def.keyPass90: Passes that lead directly to a shot, per 90 minutes.
def.chances90: Clear chances set up for a teammate, per 90 minutes.
def.xgPer90: Expected goals: quality of shooting chances, per 90 minutes.
def.xaPer90: Expected assists: quality of chances set up, per 90 minutes.
def.press90: Pressures that win the ball or force an error, per 90 minutes.
def.interc90: Opposition passes cut out, per 90 minutes.
def.possLost90: Possession lost, per 90 minutes (lower is better).
def.fouls90: Fouls committed, per 90 minutes (lower is better).
def.mistakes: Mistakes leading to an opposition goal (lower is better).
def.xgPrevented90: Goals the keeper prevented relative to shot quality faced, per 90 minutes.
def.savePct: Share of shots on target saved.
def.points90: Points won per match by the team with this player on the pitch.

trend.title: Progress since {{date}}
trend.noneUp: Nobody clearly improved over the period.
trend.noneDown: Nobody clearly declined over the period.
trend.help: Recent period (stats since that date) compared with the season up to it. A player needs at least 180 minutes on each side. Threshold: 3 points for a percentage, 15% for a per-90 stat. Shows whether training and instructions pay off.
trend.wait: The comparison appears once Simloom has at least one in-game week of snapshots with stats (the first is from {{date}}). Keep playing with the plugin on.
trend.waitNone: No snapshots with match stats yet.

dbSearch.title: Search the whole database
dbSearch.teaser: Find signings among every player in the save, by your criteria (position, age, ability, wage).
dbSearch.help: Read-only access to the FM27 database, on demand, with the save open. CA/PA and attributes are the game's true values, not what your scouts know. Results are ranked by what they add to the project XI. Nationality and division: one or more name parts separated by commas. League level: the game's reputation (Premier League 189, LaLiga 180, Championship 136).
dbSearch.none: No player matches. Widen the criteria.

f.usefulOnly: Only those who strengthen the XI

pageIntro.squad: Every first-team player, sortable by level, condition, contract or wage; then the dressing room and your loaned-out players.
pageIntro.analysis: The squad diagnosis, each player's fit for each position, match statistics and progression.
pageIntro.tactic: The best formation and starting eleven available today, the starter and backups in each position, then tactical effectiveness.
pageIntro.opponent: The next opponent, then the fixtures and who to rotate based on fatigue.
pageIntro.mercato: Step 4: who to let go, which youngsters to keep, then your shortlist ranked by what each player would add to the project.
pageIntro.finances: Budgets and board expectations, the wage bill, then contract expiries to plan for.

compat.title: Best project role: {{fit}} · best role overall: {{best}}
compat.noPosition: No position of the project formation within reach
compat.help: Does the profile suit the game plan? We compare the rating in the best role of the project eleven with the best possible rating at the player's positions. Project ✓: gap of 0.3 star at most; Project ~: up to 0.8 star; Off project: more, or no position in the formation. This measures profile, not level: don't invest time (training, renewal, transfer) in an off-project player.

decide.help: Contracts ending within six months, the ones FM27 messages you about. For each: the decision to take in the game, then why (place in today's and the project eleven, fit with the game plan, age, potential).
decide.legend: Renew: starter, useful backup under 29, or promising youngster who suits the project. Renew 1 year: starter aged 31+, backup aged 29-30, or off-project starter while you find better. Sell in January: no place in either eleven or off-project profile, but has market value. Let go: same without value, or backup aged 31+.

evo.title: Development plan
evo.help: What your tactic and squad become over the next transfer windows if you follow Simloom: advised departures and contract expiries applied, players aged by their measured progression. The same base is kept unless another tactic is clearly better, and instructions are added as the group improves. No signing is invented: a position to recruit stays open until someone signs.
evo.perPlayerHelp: Group tactical ability {{ability}} for {{need}} wanted: the less it covers, the less we load the players.
evo.changeTip: The change falls on the window: use pre-season or the winter break to work on the new tactic before matches.
evo.recruit: Still to recruit for the project: {{list}}
evo.foot: Windows computed from the league restart month (Training settings). Provisional costs chosen by Simloom: changing tactic needs a half-star gain; a style too complex for the group loses up to half a star.

abilities.help: Reads your squad's real CA and PA (out of 200) from FM27's memory, read-only, once per game date. The game's stars are relative to the squad; CA/PA gives a fixed scale for progression and potential. Note: PA is a value the game hides from you.

dec.help: What Simloom advises, most urgent first. You remain the judge: click a card for details.
dec.none: Nothing to decide right now: keep your base tactic and today's XI.

action.letGo: Let {{names}} leave at the end of the contract

why.potentialPa: PA {{pa}}: he can overtake the starter in his position (CA {{ca}}).
why.potential: {{stars}} ★ potential per your staff, relative to the current squad.
why.surplus: Doesn't play and has no place in the project ({{age}} years old).
why.smallGain: {{other}} would only be {{gain}} ★ better: not enough to lose tactical understanding ({{need}} ★ needed).
why.bigGain: At least {{need}} ★ better than {{other}}: worth the learning time. Switch during pre-season or the winter break.
why.weakSlot: The best player for this position only reaches {{fit}}% suitability in the project.
why.emptySlot: Nobody in the squad covers this project position.
why.blocked: Promising youngster without game time here: a loan will help him develop.

unless.bigGain: Review if the gap exceeds {{need}} ★ (injuries, signings).

pz2.error: This game's Zoologix register could not be opened. Restart Simloom, then try again.
